title: Introduction to Amazon Elastic Container Registry - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a fully managed AWS Docker registry service that enables secure storage, management and deployment of container images. ECR is highly scalable and reliable, allowing you to scale resources up or down based on your requirements.

  • It uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to enable resource-based permissions for private
  • Docker repositories and through the Docker command-line interface (CLI), you can push, pull, and manage images.

Components

Amazon ECR consists of the following key components:

  1. Each AWS account has access to the Amazon ECR registry. Within the registry, you can create image repositories and store container images.
  2. Before pushing and pulling images, your Docker client must authenticate to Amazon ECR registries as an AWS user. The AWS CLI provides a command called "get-login" which provides authentication credentials to be passed to Docker.
  3. Docker images are contained within Amazon ECR image repositories. Each repository can hold multiple versions of container images.
  4. Repository policies enable users to control access to their repositories and the images within them. Policies are managed through IAM and determine who can push, pull, or delete images.
  5. Container images stored in ECR can be easily pushed or pulled. Images can be used on your local system or referenced in Amazon ECS task definitions and EKS deployments.

Create a ECR

Step 1 : First, open the AWS Management Console and search for Amazon ECR.

  • Open Amazon ECR.
  • Select Repositories from the left navigation menu.
  • Click Create repository.
  • Enter a repository name, for example: 
gfg

Step 2: Push the Docker Image to Amazon ECR. Once the ECR repository has been created, the next step is to push the Docker image to the repository. This involves authenticating Docker with ECR, tagging the image, and pushing it.

Authenticate Docker with Amazon ECR

Click on Push commands to view all the commands to connect your ECR with local and push your image to ECR

Run the following command:

aws ecr get-login-password --region <AWS-REGION> | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <AWS-ACCOUNT-ID>.dkr.ecr.<AWS-REGION>.amazonaws.com

Features

  • Supports image versioning using tags
  • Automatically removes old images with lifecycle policies
  • Scans images for security vulnerabilities
  • Integrates with ECS, EKS, and AWS Lambda
  • Supports cross-region image replication
  • Provides both public and private repositories

Benefits

  • AWS manages the infrastructure, so users can focus on application development.
  • ECR can handle growing workloads while providing reliable image storage.
  • Supports IAM permissions and encryption for secure image access.
  • Helps developers quickly push and pull container images.
  • Works smoothly with ECS, EKS, and AWS Lambda.
  • Users pay only for the storage and usage they consume.
  • Teams can easily share and manage container images together.
  • Allows simple organization and version management of images.

Use Cases

Use CaseDescriptionHow ECR Helps
Containerized Application DeploymentStoring Docker images for applications deployed on ECS or EKS.ECR securely stores images that can be easily pulled during deployment.
Microservices ArchitectureManaging multiple microservices in containers.ECR stores and manages separate images for each microservice.
CI/CD PipelinesAutomating build and deployment processes.ECR integrates with CI/CD tools for smooth image deployment.
Hybrid and Multi-Cloud DeploymentRunning applications across AWS and on-premises systems.ECR allows images to be accessed from different environments.
Image Versioning and RollbackManaging different image versions.ECR supports tagging and rollback of container images.
Security and ComplianceMaintaining secure container images.ECR scans images for vulnerabilities before deployment.
Private Docker Image StorageKeeping container images private and secure.ECR provides secure private repositories with IAM access control.
Scalable Image StorageStoring large numbers of container images.ECR automatically scales storage as needed.
DevOps WorkflowImproving developer productivity and collaboration.ECR simplifies pushing, pulling, and managing Docker images.

Amazon ECR Pricing

Amazon ECR pricing is based on storage usage, data transfer, and additional features like encryption and image signing.

Pricing ComponentCurrent PricingDetails
Private Repository Storage$0.10/GB-monthStorage of container images in private repositories.
Public Repository Storage50 GB/month freePublic repository storage is free up to 50 GB/month.
Private Repository Data Transfer InFreeNo charge for data transferred into ECR.
Private Repository Data Transfer Out$0.09/GB*Applies to applicable data transfer out, such as transfers to the internet.
Public Repository Data Transfer500 GB/month free*Anonymous transfers are free up to 500 GB/month; authenticated transfers get up to 5 TB/month free.
ECR → AWS Services in Same RegionFreeData transfer between ECR and services such as EC2, ECS, Fargate, and Lambda in the same Region is free.
Image SigningAdditional charges may applyManaged signing can automatically sign images pushed to ECR.
